saints.name: St. Katharine Drexel
saints.title: Virgin, Foundress of the Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament
saints.shortBlurb: A Philadelphia heiress who gave her fortune to found schools and missions for Native and African Americans…
biography: Born in Philadelphia on 26 November 1858 into the banking family of Francis Anthony Drexel, Katharine lost her mother within weeks of her birth and grew up in a household where alms were distributed daily. Travel in the West opened her eyes to the misery of Native Americans.

In 1887, in an audience with Pope Leo XIII, she begged him to send missionaries to the Indians; he answered, "Why not become a missionary yourself?" She entered the Sisters of Mercy in 1889 and in February 1891 founded the Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament for Indians and Colored People, which she governed until 1937.

From her inherited fortune she financed more than sixty schools and missions for Native and African Americans, and from 1915 built up work in New Orleans that became Xavier University of Louisiana, the only historically Black Catholic university in the country.

She died at Bensalem, Pennsylvania, on 3 March 1955, aged ninety-six. Beatified in 1988 and canonized by Pope John Paul II on 1 October 2000, she was the first native-born American citizen declared a saint. Having spent her fortune on the oppressed, she is invoked as patron of racial justice and of philanthropists.
saints.knownFor: Devoting her inheritance and life to the education of Native and African Americans.
